subject: songbird data with questions on adjustment selection and variance

messages.subject: songbird data with questions on adjustment selection and variance
parts:
I am using distance to analyze transects to determine avian abundance =
(analyzed in clusters) in agricultural fields. I have tried multiple =
truncations, groupings, and models and have come up with 'best' models for =
each treatment/time period. I originally used the default 'sequential' =
for adjustment terms and 'estimate variance empirically' for variance. =
Should I go back and try the 'forward' adjustment selection and bootstrap =
for variance? I know Distance Sampling (pg120) recommends evaluating the =
bootstrap on the final model, but is this always a superior method of =
estimating variance? I have noticed, for the few that I have already =
tried, that the CV for bootstrap is higher than the CV for the analytical. =
Is this normal? Thanks for the help.

Sandy Cederbaum
University of Georgia
